From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Performance targets & next steps

Hi Emily / Mike —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can scope the customer-led load test: 

1) SLO / targets
- P50 latency target: <= 150ms (text-generation, avg prompt 120 tokens)
- P95 latency target: <= 450ms
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s across 6 concurrent workers
- Streaming: yes — customers will use SSE for partial token streaming (important for tail latency)

2) Test plan items (what Redwood will provide)
- k6 script (attached) that simulates production prompt mix and streaming behavior
- short-lived test accounts and API keys scoped to the Acme tenant
- IP allowlist file and region-specific endpoints for the test window
- Support on ramping schedule and monitoring dashboard (we will share Grafana link)

3) What we need from Acme
- Confirm test window (2–3 hour window preferred) and timezone
- Confirm a list of external IPs for your load agents (we will also spin up our infra if needed)
- Provide any top-traffic prompt templates you want prioritized in the script

Proposed next steps:
- I will attach the initial k6 script and the load test plan. Please verify the prompt mix by EOD Friday so we can finalize scripts.
- Marissa will coordinate the test window and monitoring.
- Aditya will provision test API keys once we have the confirmed window and IPs.

Attachments: k6-script-v2.js (stub), load-test-plan.pdf (stub), ip-allowlist.txt (stub)

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales (Performance) | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is exactly what we discussed. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- The streaming requirement is critical for our customer-facing UX; we care about first-chunk time as much as end-to-end. Can the k6 script simulate partial chunk delays?
- Our preferred test window is Tues 2 Mar 2027, 02:00–05:00 UTC (off-peak for our region). Is that workable for your team?
- We will be running our own Locust agents from our infra plus one managed runner from Redwood for cross-validation. I'll send the IP list in a follow-up.

Also: can you scope the test to 3 concurrency groups: 1) low (10 req/s), 2) medium (60 req/s), 3) high (120 req/s) with 15-minute ramps between stages? We'll simulate a 70/20/10 prompt distribution in the script.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Zhang
Principal PM, AI Platform | Acme Corp
